audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer describes a different champion as the owner. It repeatedly names 'Starsurge', 'Voidlink (E)', 'your stars are too spread out', 'your stars fully surround her at max stack' and 'your stacked star orbit'. None of these are current Aurelion Sol abilities. Separately, Vanguard's Edge is described as an ability that 'dashes, stuns, and shreds resistances' in two places.
audit.why: Current Aurelion Sol has Breath of Light (Q, 750, channel), Astral Flight (W), the black hole (E, 750, execute) and Falling Star (R, 1250). Starsurge was the pre-rework Q and Voidlink is not his ability at all — a reader is being told to press buttons that do not exist. And Riot's text for Vanguard's Edge is unambiguous: it fires blades that damage and Mark, then form a slowing wall. It does not dash, does not stun, and shreds nothing. The stun is Flawless Duet (E), 16s at rank 1. Telling a player Irelia's ultimate is the stun means they dodge the wrong cast at the moment that decides the lane.
audit.corrected: Owner abilities corrected to Breath of Light / black hole / Falling Star throughout the content layer. Vanguard's Edge corrected to Mark plus retreat-cutting wall; the stun reattributed to Flawless Duet with its 16s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side said Irelia while win[5] said Aurelion Sol, and phases[6].side said Skill while win[6] said Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: Two rows rendering different answers, in a 49.27% lane over 615 games where the item spike is exactly where it turns.
audit.corrected: Both full-layer sides set to Aurelion Sol to match content.

audit.corrected: Named Rod of Ages in both, consistent with report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' — wrong pronoun, no reason.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals her on every dash and refreshes on Marked targets, so the sustain compounds with the reset. That is the reason Grievous Wounds matters here and it was never given.
audit.corrected: Named Bladesurge and its per-dash heal.

edits.after: Vanguard's Edge does not stun — it Marks you and drops a slowing wall behind you. The stun is Flawless Duet, 16s at rank 1, and that is the cast which actually starts her kill.

edits.after: Irelia unlocks the Flawless Duet into Bladesurge all-in at level 3, and Breath of Light's channel is far too slow to punish a 600-range dash before she is already on top of you.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are already rough because Irelia's Bladesurge resets off minions let her jump you from max range while your stars are still orbiting wide and doing little single-target damage, so you're mostly playing for safe CS and dodging her Q chain rather than trading. By levels 3-5 she has her full Q-E combo online and the all-in only gets scarier as her resistances climb, so play from max Starsurge range and never let her land two Q stacks back to back.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are rough because Bladesurge refreshes on any Marked target or kill, so she chains minion dashes onto you while Breath of Light needs a slow channel to answer at all. Play for safe CS and never stand on the line between the two converging blades of Flawless Duet. By levels 3-5 she has the full E-into-Q all-in and it only gets scarier as her resistances climb, so farm from the edge of your 750 beam range and never let a Mark stick.

edits.before: Level 6 is her single scariest spike in the whole game: Vanguard's Edge dashes to you, stuns, and shreds your resistances, and you have zero panic button to answer it since your own ultimate isn't a gap-closer or a peel tool. Bank your E for the stun-interrupt or a last-second disengage, keep vision up for jungle help, and treat this window as pure survival rather than a fight you can win.
edits.after: Level 6 is her scariest spike, but not for the reason you would guess: Vanguard's Edge Marks you and walls off your retreat, and it is Flawless Duet — 16 seconds at rank 1 — that lands the stun which starts the kill. Bank Astral Flight for the disengage rather than the poke, keep vision up for jungle help, and treat this window as pure survival rather than a fight you can win.

edits.before: Once you finish your core mana/burn item your Q comet clear and stacked star orbit finally out-damage her sustained combo, and by two items your ultimate deletes her from a screen away before she can even flash into dash range. From here you scale into full lane dominance and teamfight relevance while her kit caps out with nothing left to punish your range advantage.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages lands, the black hole's execute plus banked stardust finally out-damage her sustained combo, and by two items Falling Star reaches from 1250 — a screen further than Bladesurge's 600 can answer, even through Flash. From here you scale into lane control and teamfight relevance while her kit caps out with nothing left to punish your range.

edits.after: - Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 — two blades that converge, so stay off the line between them and her dive has no stun. - Bladesurge refreshes on a Marked target, making a landed Mark a free dash. - Budget W for emergencies.

edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. Rod of Ages rush (or Seraph's), then Archangel's, Liandry's, Rabadon's. Zhonya's vs dive comps. Bladesurge heals her every dash — anti-heal before extended trades.

notes: This is the worst matchup in my slice and the failure is not a typo — the whole content layer was written against a different Aurelion Sol. 'Starsurge' is his pre-rework Q and 'Voidlink' is not his ability in any version; both were being given to the player as buttons to press. I corrected every instance reachable through a writable path. Worth checking whether other aurelionsol matchups carry the same pre-rework text, since this reads like inherited content that predates his rework rather than a one-off error. Note also: enemyKit W (Defiant Dance) reduces PHYSICAL damage only per Riot's text, which is why it does nothing against your beam — I used that, and it is the one piece of good news in the matchup.
